claims.text: 现有证据仅包含一篇关于nnU-Net的摘要，未检索到任何MedSAM相关段落，因此无法基于所提供证据直接比较MedSAM与nnU-Net的差异。
limitations: 仅有摘要级证据，且缺少MedSAM一侧的任何描述。

claims.text: nnU-Net被描述为一个稳健、自适应的框架，基于2D和3D原生U-Net构建，其主张是去除许多网络设计中多余的复杂结构，转而聚焦于影响性能与泛化性的架构、预处理、训练和推理选择。
limitations: 来自摘要，未提供具体实现细节。

claims.text: nnU-Net在医学分割十项全能挑战中评估，覆盖十个学科、不同实体、影像模态、图像几何和数据集规模，且数据集之间不允许人工调整；据报告，投稿时其在所有类别和七个第一阶段任务（BrainTumour的类别1除外）上取得最高平均Dice分数。
limitations: 为投稿时点的在线排行榜结果，属摘要报告，未给出具体数值。

claims.text: 由于缺少MedSAM的方法、训练数据或评测结果描述，无法判断两者在提示方式、数据需求、泛化性或精度上的差异；任何此类对比在此证据集下均属推测。
limitations: 推断基于证据缺失，而非对MedSAM的直接观察。

openalex_record.title: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation
openalex_record.abstract: The U-Net was presented in 2015. With its straight-forward and successful architecture it quickly evolved to a commonly used benchmark in medical image segmentation. The adaptation of the U-Net to novel problems, however, comprises several degrees of freedom regarding the exact architecture, preprocessing, training and inference. These choices are not independent of each other and substantially impact the overall performance. The present paper introduces the nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), which refers to a robust and self-adapting framework on the basis of 2D and 3D vanilla U-Nets. We argue the strong case for taking away superfluous bells and whistles of many proposed network designs and instead focus on the remaining aspects that make out the performance and generalizability of a method. We evaluate the nnU-Net in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge, which measures segmentation performance in ten disciplines comprising distinct entities, image modalities, image geometries and dataset sizes, with no manual adjustments between datasets allowed. At the time of manuscript submission, nnU-Net achieves the highest mean dice scores across all classes and seven phase 1 tasks (except class 1 in BrainTumour) in the online leaderboard of the challenge.

sources.title: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation

evidence.text: The U-Net was presented in 2015. With its straight-forward and successful architecture it quickly evolved to a commonly used benchmark in medical image segmentation. The adaptation of the U-Net to novel problems, however, comprises several degrees of freedom regarding the exact architecture, preprocessing, training and inference. These choices are not independent of each other and substantially impact the overall performance. The present paper introduces the nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), which refers to a robust and self-adapting framework on the basis of 2D and 3D vanilla U-Nets. We argue the strong case for taking away superfluous bells and whistles of many proposed network designs and instead focus on the remaining aspects that make out the performance and generalizability of a method. We evaluate the nnU-Net in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge, which measures segmentation performance in ten disciplines comprising distinct entities, image modalities, image geometries and dataset sizes, with no manual adjustments between datasets allowed. At the time of manuscript submission, nnU-Net achieves the highest mean dice scores across all classes and seven phase 1 tasks (except class 1 in BrainTumour) in the online leaderboard of the challenge.

records.title: Segment anything in medical images
records.abstract: Medical image segmentation is a critical component in clinical practice, facilitating accurate diagnosis, treatment planning, and disease monitoring. However, existing methods, often tailored to specific modalities or disease types, lack generalizability across the diverse spectrum of medical image segmentation tasks. Here we present MedSAM, a foundation model designed for bridging this gap by enabling universal medical image segmentation. The model is developed on a large-scale medical image dataset with 1,570,263 image-mask pairs, covering 10 imaging modalities and over 30 cancer types. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation on 86 internal validation tasks and 60 external validation tasks, demonstrating better accuracy and robustness than modality-wise specialist models. By delivering accurate and efficient segmentation across a wide spectrum of tasks, MedSAM holds significant potential to expedite the evolution of diagnostic tools and the personalization of treatment plans.

records.title: MedSAM-U: Uncertainty-Guided Auto Multi-Prompt Adaptation for Reliable MedSAM
records.journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
records.abstract: The Medical Segment Anything Model (MedSAM) has demonstrated strong performance in medical image segmentation, attracting increasing attention in the medical imaging domain. However, as with many prompt-based segmentation models, its performance is highly sensitive to the type and location of input prompts. This sensitivity often leads to suboptimal segmentation outcomes and necessitates labor-intensive manual prompt tuning, which hampers both efficiency and robustness. To address this challenge, this paper proposes MedSAM-U, an uncertainty-guided framework designed to automatically refine prompt inputs and enhance segmentation reliability. Specifically, a Multi-Prompt Adapter is integrated into MedSAM, resulting in MPA-MedSAM, which enables the model to effectively accommodate diverse multi-prompt inputs. An uncertainty estimation module is then introduced to evaluate the reliability of the prompts and their initial segmentation results. Based on this, a novel uncertainty-guided prompt adaptation strategy is applied to automatically generate refined prompts and more accurate segmentation outputs. The proposed MedSAM-U framework is evaluated across multiple medical imaging modalities. Experimental results on five diverse datasets demonstrate that MedSAM-U achieves consistent performance improvements ranging from 1.7% to 20.5% over the baseline MedSAM, confirming its effectiveness and practicality for robust and efficient medical image segmentation.

records.title: Evaluating a Deep Learning Foundation Model for Neuroimaging Segmentation in the Data-Rich and Data-Constrained Settings
records.journal: Proceedings on CD-ROM - International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine. Scientific Meeting and Exhibition/Proceedings of the International Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine, Scientific Meeting and Exhibition
records.abstract: Motivation: Deep learning models for segmentation require large datasets, limiting their use in clinical settings. Foundation models, which learn from non-medical images before fine-tuning for specific tasks, have emerged as a possible solution. Goal(s): We aimed to adapt and evaluate a recent foundation model, the Medical Segment Anything model (MedSAM), for neuroanatomy segmentation. Approach: Using the Human Connectome Project dataset, we trained MedSAM to segment 102 regions-of-interest and compared its accuracy with a baseline UNet model. Results: UNet outperformed MedSAM in almost all regions and dataset sizes, but MedSAM showed potential when training with very few MRIs. Impact: While foundation models such as MedSAM have potential for medical segmentation, they currently may not surpass traditional models when using sufficient data. In the data-limited setting, however, they can be useful when extremely little labeled data is available.

records.title: Development and validation of an autonomous artificial intelligence agent for clinical decision-making in oncology
records.abstract: Clinical decision-making in oncology is complex, requiring the integration of multimodal data and multidomain expertise. We developed and evaluated an autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI) agent leveraging GPT-4 with multimodal precision oncology tools to support personalized clinical decision-making. The system incorporates vision transformers for detecting microsatellite instability and KRAS and BRAF mutations from histopathology slides, MedSAM for radiological image segmentation and web-based search tools such as OncoKB, PubMed and Google. Evaluated on 20 realistic multimodal patient cases, the AI agent autonomously used appropriate tools with 87.5% accuracy, reached correct clinical conclusions in 91.0% of cases and accurately cited relevant oncology guidelines 75.5% of the time. Compared to GPT-4 alone, the integrated AI agent drastically improved decision-making accuracy from 30.3% to 87.2%. These findings demonstrate that integrating language models with precision oncology and search tools substantially enhances clinical accuracy, establishing a robust foundation for deploying AI-driven personalized oncology support systems.

records.title: Point-supervised Brain Tumor Segmentation with Box-prompted MedSAM
records.abstract: Delineating lesions and anatomical structure is important for image-guided interventions. Point-supervised medical image segmentation (PSS) has great potential to alleviate costly expert delineation labeling. However, due to the lack of precise size and boundary guidance, the effectiveness of PSS often falls short of expectations. Although recent vision foundational models, such as the medical segment anything model (MedSAM), have made significant advancements in bounding-box-prompted segmentation, it is not straightforward to utilize point annotation, and is prone to semantic ambiguity. In this preliminary study, we introduce an iterative framework to facilitate semantic-aware point-supervised MedSAM. Specifically, the semantic box-prompt generator (SBPG) module has the capacity to convert the point input into potential pseudo bounding box suggestions, which are explicitly refined by the prototype-based semantic similarity. This is then succeeded by a prompt-guided spatial refinement (PGSR) module that harnesses the exceptional generalizability of MedSAM to infer the segmentation mask, which also updates the box proposal seed in SBPG. Performance can be progressively improved with adequate iterations. We conducted an evaluation on BraTS2018 for the segmentation of whole brain tumors and demonstrated its superior performance compared to traditional PSS methods and on par with box-supervised methods.

records.title: Uncertainty-Aware Training for Ophthalmic Segmentation Using MedSAM
records.abstract: Purpose: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) has been applied to deep learning (DL) models to enhance not only their interpretability, but to guide model learning. This work presents Uncertainty-Aware Training (UAT), which generates uncertainty maps at train time and augments the loss function with them to allow the models to concentrate on areas of high uncertainty during learning. By highlighting uncertain pixels as requiring more scrutiny, model performance is enhanced on three ophthalmic segmentation tasks. Methods: We applied UAT to three ophthalmic segmentation, or pixel-level classification, tasks: geographic atrophy (GA), optic cup (OC), and foveal avascular zone (FAZ). UAT weighs the loss function binary cross-entropy according to uncertainty, forcing the model to focus on ambiguous areas. We experimented with output-based UQ methods, such as entropy, and post -hoc techniques like conformal prediction. UAT was evaluated on a state-of-the-art foundational model fine-tuned for these specific segmentation tasks. Results: The addition of an entropy-weighing map at loss calculation time consistently improved model performance across all three datasets, with conformal prediction using the Least Ambiguous Set-Valued Classifier version also achieving higher overall performance for GA and OC segmentation. The easy-to-integrate implementation of UAT proved feasible without significant training structure modifications. Conclusions: UAT enhances DL model performance and interpretability by focusing on uncertainty in addition to error, improving segmentation accuracy. Translational Relevance: UAT uses interpretable uncertainty maps to enhance DL segmentation performance. Its lightweight integration makes it practical for adoption and leads to improved model performance on ophthalmic segmentation tasks.

records.title: Comparative Analysis and Adaptation Strategies of Vision Foundation Models in Dermoscopic Image Segmentation
records.abstract: Accurate segmentation of skin lesions is of critical clinical importance for early melanoma diagnosis; however, the direct application of large foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to medical images characterized by low contrast and fuzzy boundaries remains insufficient due to substantial domain gaps. In current study, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning strategy is presented by integrating lightweight adapter modules into a frozen Vision Transformer backbone. The proposed SAM-Adapter approach was comparatively evaluated against the original SAM and MedSAM models on the publicly available ISIC2018 and HAM10000 dermoscopic datasets. Optimized with AdamW, the model achieved the highest Dice (0.9603) and IoU (0.9241) scores along with the lowest HD95 (22.57) value on the HAM10000 dataset. Validated as statistically significant via the Wilcoxon test, this approach minimized computational overhead while demonstrating superior accuracy in boundary delineation. This adapter-based framework is planned for integration into clinical decision-support systems and other medical imaging modalities.

records.title: Resolution preservation over architectural complexity: high-resolution patch-based semi-supervised learning for pancreas segmentation from CT images
records.abstract: Precise segmentation of the pancreas from computed tomography (CT) scans is critical for diagnosis and surgical planning but remains challenging due to the organ’s small volume (<0.5% of the abdomen), high anatomical variability, and low contrast with surround­ing tissues. Conventional deep learning methods typically downsample inputs to fit GPU memory, destroying fine-grained boundary information essential for small-organ delinea­tion. This study proposes a high-resolution patch-based framework that preserves native CT resolution (512 × 512) through 256 × 256 patch extraction with domain-specific Hounsfield unit (HU) windowing. A lightweight 2D U-Net (7.8M parameters) achieves 0.809±0.015 Dice (peak 0.849) on the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) Task07 Pancreas dataset, com­petitive with nnU-Net (0.823 Dice, 88M parameters) and far above SAM (0.705) and Med­SAM (0.439). Five-fold cross-validation across all 281 volumes yields a population-level Dice of 0.630±0.025. Integrating uncertainty-aware mean teacher (UA-MT) semi-supervised learning recovers 99.3% of supervised performance using only 50% of labelled data, with reproducible results across three seeds (σ = 0.012). On 80 external TCIA volumes, UA-MT (0.603 Dice) out­performs the supervised model (0.544), demonstrating superior cross-domain generalisation.

records.title: Explainable trust aware graph learning for skin lesion classification with uncertainty estimation
records.abstract: TrustGraphNet integrates trust-weighted graph propagation, probabilistic uncertainty estimation, graph-based explanation signals, and a composite Trust Reliability Index (TRI) for dermoscopic skin-lesion classification. We evaluate the framework on executed HAM10000 (1,042 images; seven classes) and MILK10k (2,501 images; 11 classes) subsets using lesion-level separation where metadata permit. On the corrected 203-image HAM10000 test set, TrustGraphNet achieved a three-seed mean accuracy of 0.608 ± 0.010 versus 0.571 ± 0.048 for a same-budget CNN, but had lower mean macro-F1 (0.194 ± 0.073 vs. 0.256 ± 0.031), AUROC (0.779 ± 0.016 vs. 0.802 ± 0.014), and less favorable calibration. The historical TRI means were 0.9547 for correct and 0.9593 for incorrect predictions and therefore do not establish error discrimination. To address reviewer-requested analyses without misrepresenting unavailable historical per-case outputs, we additionally performed an independently trained lesion-disjoint reproduction on the verified 1,042-image/857-lesion cohort using a frozen 689/150/203 split. In that reproduction, uncertainty detected prediction errors with AUROC 0.767 (95% bootstrap CI 0.702–0.830) at 64 × 64 and 0.791 (0.725–0.852) at 128 × 128; validation-selected melanoma logit adjustment increased test melanoma recall from 0.385 to 0.692 at 64 × 64, with accuracy changing from 0.616 to 0.606; and equal-budget deletion produced a larger probability decrease for high-trust than random nodes (0.0508 vs. 0.0055). Increasing resolution to 128 × 128 did not uniformly improve classification. These findings support a diagnostic evaluation of trust-aware graph learning and identify limitations in the original TRI, calibration, class sensitivity, and reproducibility rather than establishing clinical reliability.

records.title: A comprehensive study of skin lesion segmentation and classification using deep learning techniques
records.abstract: Deep learning has become an important computational approach in dermatology because it enables automated segmentation and classification of skin lesions. Manual dermoscopic analysis is time-consuming and depends on specialist expertise, with potential inter-observer variability. There is a need to develop reliable computer-aided diagnostic tools. This structured narrative review covers journal papers published mainly from 2018 to 2026 on skin lesion analysis with focus on image preprocessing, benchmark datasets, conventional machine learning approaches, convolutional neural networks, U-Net architectures, transfer learning approaches, Vision Transformers, attention-based models, ensemble solutions, and hybrid segmentation–classification systems. Building on present reviews covering individual tasks as well as broader segmentation–classification pipelines, the present work provides a critical development-to-deployment analysis connecting dataset characteristics, preprocessing, segmentation, classification, evaluation, explainability, robustness, fairness, computational requirements, and clinical applicability. The paper describes widely used evaluation metrics and explains why results obtained across different datasets, partitions, and experimental setups should not be directly compared. Major open problems include class imbalance, data bias, domain shift, limited representation of diverse skin tones, inadequate external validation, computational requirements, and limited explainability of efficient models. Emerging trends such as self-supervised learning, Transformers, foundation models, explainable AI, federated learning, and multi-modal clinical data are reviewed as well. The review offers practical advice to researchers and clinicians on how to approach the preprocessing, segmentation, classification, and evaluation of skin lesions and highlights priorities in developing clinically reliable skin lesion analysis systems.

records.title: Methodological audit and empirical evaluation of a lightweight whole-volume 3D CNN for preterm brain injury classification
records.abstract: Abstract This study uses methodological auditing to evaluate a proof-of-concept engineering pipeline for classifying radiological severity groups of preterm brain injury (BI) from T2-weighted MRI in the dHCP cohort. Its primary contribution is methodology-driven empirical discovery rather than a new neural-network architecture. GloResNet combines a standard ResNet-10 backbone, MedicalNet initialization, whole-volume array resizing, mixup, and array-axis-0-reversal probability averaging, hereafter referred to as axis-0-reversal averaging; no new CNN block is proposed. The audit identifies concrete mechanisms by which small-cohort imaging results can be overstated, including unit-of-analysis drift, fold-assignment non-traceability, post hoc model-selection bias, and ranking across incompatible evaluation protocols. Building on this framework, we report the first fair, traceable comparison between a de novo trained Vision Transformer (ViT) and a domain-adapted lightweight 3D CNN on a public preterm brain injury dataset. When all sources of bias are controlled, the lightweight CNN achieves comparable or superior performance to ViT, challenging the prevailing assumption that larger, more complex architectures are always preferable in low-data regimes. Applying the audit to the historical evidence also showed that the archived GloResNet mean fold accuracy of $$69.12 \pm 7.42\%$$ was calculated over 180 scan records from 128 subjects, including repeated scans, without retained subject identifiers or out-of-fold predictions. The historical archive is therefore reported separately from the fair, traceable server-side comparison. A separate, auditable subject-level input-representation experiment did not demonstrate superiority of whole-volume input. The resulting minimum reporting standard requires an explicit statistical unit, traceable subject-level folds, retained out-of-fold predictions, prespecified selection rules, and transparent comparator conditions. These internal estimates do not establish clinical screening performance or external generalizability. The source code is available at https://github.com/ICL-SUST/GloResNet-Preterm-Brain

records.title: VTRL-Med: Progressive Visual Refinement with Topology-Guided Regularization for Medical Image Clustering
records.abstract: Deep clustering offers a promising approach for analyzing large unlabeled medical image datasets, yet prevailing methods still face two limitations: they may neglect class-agnostic structural priors that capture object boundaries and regions, and they do not explicitly encode topological patterns (e.g., connectivity and holes). These sources of information play distinct and complementary roles: visual-structural features provide the primary discriminative representation for clustering, while topological features provide additional global geometric cues for residual visual ambiguities. We introduce VTRL-Med, a progressive visual-structural learning framework with topology-guided regularization for medical image clustering. VTRL-Med first adapts the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to extract image features that retain structural cues inherited from mask-supervised pretraining. It then generates reliable pseudo-labels through a two-step filtering process that combines prototype-based selection with k-nearest neighbor consistency validation. Finally, it progressively refines the visual branch while an auxiliary topology branch, constructed from persistent homology (PH) descriptors, provides additional geometric regularization during training. Across 13 medical image benchmarks, VTRL-Med achieves state-of-the-art clustering performance, improving average accuracy by 4.48% over existing methods. On three representative datasets, topology-guided regularization further improves accuracy by 1.3--4.3% over visual refinement alone.

records.title: Polyp-VSSD: A Pre-trained Transformer with Local-Global Joint VSSD Decoding for Polyp Segmentation
records.abstract: Early detection of colorectal polyps is essential for preventing colorectal cancer, making accurate polyp segmentation a key component in computer-aided diagnosis systems. However, existing endoscopic segmentation methods often exhibit limited representational capacity and insufficient integration of global and local contextual information. To address these limitations, we propose Polyp-VSSD, a novel local-global joint decoding framework built upon a pre-trained Transformer backbone for high-precision polyp segmentation. Polyp-VSSD leverages the strong feature expressiveness of large-scale visual pre-training and unifies global semantic modeling with local fine-grained reconstruction to enhance segmentation fidelity. Extensive experiments on multiple public endoscopic datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both Dice and IoU. On the EndoScene dataset, Polyp-VSSD achieves mIoU and mDice scores of 0.903 and 0.946, respectively, highlighting its robustness and strong generalization capability. This work presents an effective and scalable solution for intelligent endoscopic image analysis.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
records.abstract: Purpose: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status is a key biomarker relevant for prognostication and treatment decision making in metastatic breast cancer. Thus, the aim of this work was to explore whether HER2 status can be predicted directly from whole-brain post-contrast T1-weighted (T1w) MRI scans in breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM) using deep learning, and whether providing explicit tumour segmentation information improves prediction. Methods: Using the publicly available BCBM-Radiogenomics dataset, we analysed 135 patients, including 70 HER2+ and 65 HER2- patients. Three approaches were implemented and evaluated: a conventional radiomics model, a simple fully convolutional network (SFCN) using T1w MRI scans alone, and an SFCN using T1w MRI scans with an expert-derived tumour mask as an additional input channel. Results: The radiomics model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.602 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.528--0.677) while the SFCN achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.667 (95% CI, 0.63--0.71) using T1w MRI scans alone, which increased to 0.692 (95% CI, 0.58--0.81) when an explicit tumour mask was additionally provided. Conclusion: However, the modest performance across all approaches demonstrates the difficulty of predicting HER2 status from structural MRI scans alone. The difference between the segmentation-free and mask-guided SFCN models suggests that much of the predictive signal captured by the deep-learning model may be learned directly from whole-brain T1w MRI without requiring explicit tumour delineation. These findings support further investigation of segmentation-free deep-learning approaches as a potential non-invasive strategy to support HER2 status determination in BCBM.

records.title: MedCaseAgent: From Multimodal Clinical Evidence to Rare Disease Case Reports
records.abstract: Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated potential in clinical documentation, generating the rigorous, evidence-based reasoning required for unprecedented, atypical, and rare disease case reports remains a significant challenge. We present MedCaseAgent, an end-to-end agentic reasoning paradigm that bridges this gap by synthesizing publication-quality reports from unstructured clinical notes. MedCaseAgent leverages a hierarchical structure, integrating patient-level data mining with iterative, tool-integrated reasoning. By dynamically querying medical literature and knowledge bases, the agent maintains high clinical fidelity and assesses case novelty. The framework is inherently modular, supporting various backbone LLMs in a plug-and-play fashion. To facilitate this research, we release MedCase-150K, a large-scale multimodal clinical case-report corpus, and MedCase-Bench, a robust temporally held-out evaluation suite. We also introduce an open-source model post-trained from Qwen3.5-9B and optimized specifically for this task. Under both LLM-judged and rule-based evaluation, MedCaseAgent outperforms existing general-purpose and specialized medical LLMs and agents. Blinded expert reviews and ablations further support the system's clinical relevance and evidence grounding.

records.title: Contrast-Gated Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of MedSAM for Skin-Tone-Robust Lesion Segmentation
records.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.abstract: Overview CG-MedSAM investigates contrast-conditioned parameter-efficient adaptation of MedSAM for skin-lesion segmentation across skin tones and imperfect bounding-box prompts. The project introduces residual bottleneck adapters modulated by a contrast signal computed within the prompt region. Research scope The manuscript evaluates segmentation quality, prompt perturbations, skin-tone subgroup performance, and contrast-conditioning ablations on ISIC 2018 and sDDI. Experimental findings and limitations should be interpreted using the manuscript and repository documentation. Supporting materials Project repository This deposit contains the author manuscript sourced from repository commit 1b73ab5b1bffa9a16dcbacacf8bc03a3ec42a433, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Datasets and model weights are not included. No journal acceptance or peer-review status is asserted by this deposit.

records.title: nnU-Net: Self-adapting Framework for U-Net-Based Medical Image Segmentation
records.abstract: The U-Net was presented in 2015. With its straight-forward and successful architecture it quickly evolved to a commonly used benchmark in medical image segmentation. The adaptation of the U-Net to novel problems, however, comprises several degrees of freedom regarding the exact architecture, preprocessing, training and inference. These choices are not independent of each other and substantially impact the overall performance. The present paper introduces the nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), which refers to a robust and self-adapting framework on the basis of 2D and 3D vanilla U-Nets. We argue the strong case for taking away superfluous bells and whistles of many proposed network designs and instead focus on the remaining aspects that make out the performance and generalizability of a method. We evaluate the nnU-Net in the context of the Medical Segmentation Decathlon challenge, which measures segmentation performance in ten disciplines comprising distinct entities, image modalities, image geometries and dataset sizes, with no manual adjustments between datasets allowed. At the time of manuscript submission, nnU-Net achieves the highest mean dice scores across all classes and seven phase 1 tasks (except class 1 in BrainTumour) in the online leaderboard of the challenge.

records.title: nnU-Net: Breaking the Spell on Successful Medical Image Segmentation.
records.abstract:
Fueled by the diversity of datasets, semantic segmentation is a popular
subfield in medical image analysis with a vast number of new methods being
proposed each year. This ever-growing jungle of methodologies, however, becomes
increasingly impenetrable. At the same time, many proposed methods fail to
generalize beyond the experiments they were demonstrated on, thus hampering the
process of developing a segmentation algorithm on a new dataset. Here we
present nnU-Net ('no-new-Net'), a framework that automatically adapts itself to
any given new dataset. While this process was completely human-driven so far,
we make a first attempt to automate necessary adaptations such as
preprocessing, the exact patch size, batch size, and inference settings based
on the properties of a given dataset. Remarkably, nnU-Net strips away the
architectural bells and whistles that are typically proposed in the literature
and relies on just a simple U-Net architecture embedded in a robust training
scheme. Out of the box, nnU-Net achieves state of the art performance on six
well-established segmentation challenges. Source code is available at
https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnunet.

records.title: Efficient nnU-Net for Brain Tumor Segmentation
records.abstract: Brain tumors are one of the leading causes of death in adults. They come in various shapes and sizes from one patient to another. Sometimes they infiltrate surrounding normal tissues, making it challenging to delineate tumor boundaries. Despite extensive research, the prognosis is still low. Accurate and timely brain tumor segmentation is critical for treatment planning and disease progression monitoring. Automatic segmentation of brain tumors using deep learning methods has been shown to produce high-quality and reproducible segmentation results. Specifically, the encoder-decoder networks, like the U-Nets, have dominated the previous BraTS Challenges because of their superior performance. Due to the importance of high-quality segmentation, most state-of-the-art models focus more on pushing the boundaries of the current methods at the expense of computational complexity. The computational budget for practical applications is minimal, requiring technological solutions that balance accuracy and available computational resources. In this study, we extended the basic U-Net model in the nnU-Net by replacing the basic 3D convolution blocks with bottleneck units utilizing depthwise-separable convolutions. Furthermore, we introduced the shuffle attention mechanism in the skip connections to compensate for the slight loss in segmentation accuracy due to a reduction in number of parameters. Extensive experimental results of the BraTS 2020 dataset reviewed that the proposed modifications achieved competitive performance at a lower computational cost.

records.title: Brain tumor segmentation with advanced nnU-Net: Pediatrics and adults tumors
records.abstract: Automated brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance (MR) images plays a crucial role in precise diagnosis and treatment monitoring in brain tumor care. Leveraging the Brain Tumor Segmentation Challenge (BraTS) dataset, this paper introduces an extended version of the nnU-Net architecture for brain tumor segmentation, addressing both adult (Glioma) and pediatric tumors . Our methodology integrates innovative approaches to enhance segmentation accuracy . We incorporate residual blocks to capture complex spatial features , attention gates to emphasize informative regions and implement the Hausdorff distance (HD) loss for boundary-based segmentation refinement. The effectiveness of each enhancement is systematically evaluated through an ablation study using different configurations on the BraTS dataset. Results from our study highlight the significance of combining residual blocks, attention gates, and HD loss, achieving the best performance with a mean Dice and HD score of 83%, 3.8 and 71%, and 8.7 for Glioma and Pediatrics datasets, respectively. This advanced nnU-Net showcases the promising potential for accurate and robust brain tumor segmentation, offering valuable insights for enhanced clinical decision-making in pediatric brain tumor care.

records.title: Application of a Fusion Model Combining MRI-VASARI Features and ADC in Predicting the Molecular Subtypes of Adult-type Diffuse Gliomas
records.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
records.abstract: Objective: To develop a machine learning model integrating MRI visually accessible Rembrandt images (VASARI) features and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) parameters for the preoperative classification of the three subtypes of adult-type diffuse glioma. Methods: This study retrospectively enrolled 206 patients with pathologically confirmed adult-type diffuse glioma and divided them by scanner type into a training set (n=114) and an independent validation set (n=92). Tumor multi-region segmentation was conducted using nnU-Net, followed by extraction of VASARI features and ADC-related parameters. Recursive feature elimination with cross-validation (RFECV), XGBoost feature importance ranking, and incremental feature selection were applied to identify the optimal feature subset, and an XGBoost-based multiclass fusion model was subsequently constructed. Results: Twelve VASARI features and four ADC parameters (ADCmin, ADCmean, rADCmin, and rADCmean) differed significantly among the three subtypes. Eight features were finally selected for model construction. The fusion model achieved accuracies of 96.49% in the training set and 80.43% in the validation set. In the validation cohort, the area under the curves (AUCs) for predicting astrocytoma and glioblastoma were 0.96 and 0.97, respectively, both higher than those of the standalone VASARI and ADC models, while the AUC for oligodendroglioma was 0.59. SHAP analysis revealed that diffusion restriction, ADC parameters, and the margin of the non-enhancing region were the primary contributors to the model. Conclusion: The XGBoost-based fusion model integrating MRI-VASARI features and ADC demonstrated a high diagnostic performance in distinguishing glioblastoma and astrocytoma, but its ability to differentiate oligodendroglioma remained limited. Future studies should incorporate additional imaging features, such as calcification, to further improve the model performance.

records.title: A multi-task learning-based network for detecting three-dimensional osteometric landmarks of the shoulder joint
records.abstract: Background Mirror-based preoperative planning for total shoulder arthroplasty relies on accurate three-dimensional (3D) localization of bony landmarks on the contralateral, anatomically intact shoulder. Manual annotation is time-consuming and shows inter- and intra-observer variability. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a multi-task deep-learning network for automated 3D bony landmark detection on contralateral shoulder CT. Methods In this single-center retrospective study, 179 patients with intact contralateral shoulder CT scans were split at the patient level into training (n = 125), validation (n = 18), and test (n = 36) sets. We developed a dual-decoder 3D BiFormer-UNet for humerus and scapula segmentation and heatmap-based localization of 14 anatomical landmarks. A cross-task feature-fusion (CtFF) module transferred bone-structural guidance from the segmentation decoder to the landmark decoder. The network was trained end-to-end using a composite loss comprising hard-negative-mining heatmap regression, a geometric structure constraint, distance-aware similarity learning, and auxiliary segmentation loss. Landmark localization was evaluated using MRE and SDR at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, while segmentation was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Per-case MRE was compared with four 3D baseline models using paired tests with Holm–Bonferroni correction. Results In the 36-case test set, the proposed model achieved an MRE of 2.1 ± 1.2 mm (95% CI, 1.7–2.5 mm) and SDRs of 72.0%, 81.8%, 90.3%, and 96.7% at thresholds of 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, and 4.0 mm, respectively. Its MRE was significantly lower than those of 3D U-Net, V-Net, 3D HRNet adaptation, and H3DE-Net (all Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted P < 0.05). On the test set, the auxiliary segmentation branch achieved mean Dice coefficients of 0.83 ± 0.05 for the humerus and 0.78 ± 0.07 for the scapula. Internally defined center landmarks, particularly the humeral head rotation center, anatomical neck center, and proximal and distal medullary canal centers, showed larger localization errors (2.3–2.6 mm) than most surface landmarks. Conclusion The proposed multi-task framework demonstrated promising 3D landmark localization performance on intact contralateral shoulder CT by integrating global anatomical context with bone-structural guidance. It may serve as an upstream localization component for mirror-based shoulder arthroplasty planning, although external validation is required before clinical use.

records.title: Interpretable and backpropagation-free Green Learning for efficient multi-task echocardiographic segmentation and classification
records.journal: APSIPA Transactions on Signal and Information Processing
records.abstract: Purpose This study develops an interpretable, backpropagation-free multi-task Green Learning (MTGL) framework for automated echocardiographic analysis. It addresses the need for reliable left ventricular (LV) segmentation and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) classification while reducing the parameter burden, energy demand and opacity associated with conventional deep learning (DL) models. The objective is to determine whether a unified feed-forward framework can deliver clinically relevant accuracy, computational efficiency and interpretable feature representations. Design/methodology/approach The framework uses a four-hop, PCA/Saab-based unsupervised VoxelHop encoder followed by a coarse-to-fine XGBoost residual-regression decoder for LV segmentation and a pooled multi-scale XGBoost classifier for three-class LVEF classification. Experiments used the predefined EchoNet-Dynamic training, validation and test partitions. MTGL was evaluated against matched 3D V-Net, 3D U-Net, 3D UNETR and 3D nnU-Net baselines using classification accuracy and balanced accuracy, and Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and intersection over union (IoU). Findings On the EchoNet-Dynamic test set, MTGL achieved 94.3% accuracy for three-class LVEF classification, and 0.912 DSC for LV segmentation, outperforming all compared baselines. It used 1.13 million parameters, versus 10.47–49.08 million for the DL comparators, and showed the lowest measured training energy use and carbon emissions. Hop ablation further showed complementary multi-scale information, with the full feature set yielding the highest classification accuracy. Originality/value Unlike end-to-end backpropagation-based DL methods, MTGL combines an unsupervised linear VoxelHop representation with task-specific XGBoost decoders in a single multi-task echocardiographic pipeline. The PCA/Saab direct current and alternating current feature decomposition enables direct inspection of learned spatial and spatiotemporal signals, linking shallow features to anatomical boundaries and deeper features to global contractile dynamics. The study therefore demonstrates that a compact, interpretable Green Learning system can jointly support LV segmentation and LVEF grouping with strong in-domain performance and lower measured training environmental cost.

records.title: An explainable hybrid transformer–CNN framework for multi-class brain tumor classification from MRI images
records.abstract: Abstract The identification of brain tumors through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) requires effective methods that provide precise results because these results determine clinical choices. The study presents a classification system based on hybrid Transformer-CNN technology which classifies brain tumors into multiple types by using tumor segmentation and deep feature extraction and explainable artificial intelligence. The preprocessing of MRI images involves several steps which include skull stripping and CLAHE-based contrast enhancement and normalization and data augmentation and resizing to create high-quality images that maintain uniformity for model input. The TransUNet architecture performs tumor region segmentation by integrating convolutional neural networks with transformer-based attention systems which enable it to recognize both nearby and distant contextual details. The system generates segmentation masks which enable region-of-interest (ROI) feature extraction through DenseNet121 that has been pretrained on ImageNet while the final classification layer gets removed and global average pooling produces discriminative feature representations. The system uses an attention-based feature refinement method to improve feature representation followed by a regularized fully connected deep classifier which includes batch normalization and dropout for four-class classification of tumors. Model interpretability is achieved using Grad-CAM++ and attention visualization, enabling clear identification of tumor-related regions and improving model transparency. Experimental evaluation demonstrates high classification performance, achieving accuracies of 98.54% for meningioma, 98.65% for glioma, 99.45% for pituitary tumors, and 99.56% for no-tumor cases. These results indicate that presented TransUNet–DenseNet121 approach offers an accurate, reliable, interpretable method for detection of brain tumors automatically from MRI scanned images.

records.title: Quantitative Measurement of White Matter Hyperintensities in Brain MRI using a Multimodal Boundary-Aware Dual-Task Segmentation Framework
records.abstract: White matter hyperintensity (WMH) subtype segmentation in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to heterogeneous lesion sizes, indistinct boundaries, and severe class imbalance. We propose a multimodal boundary-aware dual-task U-Net for segmenting periventricular (PVWMH), deep (DWMH), and subcortical (SWMH) lesions. The framework integrates FLAIR-T1-weighted feature fusion, Vision Mamba-based feature modeling, an SWMH-specific boundary loss, and auxiliary boundary detection. The method was evaluated using patient-level five-fold cross-validation on a private multicenter cohort (n = 75) and separately on 60 publicly annotated MICCAI WMH Challenge subjects for binary segmentation. On the private cohort, the proposed framework achieved an overall Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.6081 and a 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 14.80 mm, compared with 0.5638 and 18.25 mm for the FLAIR-only ablation baseline. It also improved SWMH DSC from 0.4610 with nnU-Net to 0.5215 (p = 0.008). On the public dataset, the mean binary DSC and HD95 were 0.6812 and 12.91 mm, respectively.Given the relatively large through-plane voxel spacing (8.4 mm), the framework processes 2D axial slices independently and does not explicitly model inter-slice context, which may limit its ability to characterize lesions extending across adjacent slices.

records.title: Automated segmentation and quantification of histological liver features for MASH/MASLD scoring
records.abstract: Abstract The increasing global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) creates an urgent need for objective histopathological assessment. Conventional histological approaches are time-consuming and subjective. Therefore, we propose a fully automated, deep-learning-based pipeline for the segmentation and characterisation of histological liver features of MASH/MASLD. Segmentation was applied to H&E sections from 45 mice and 44 humans with MASH/MASLD. Our qHisto (quantitative histology) method, is nnU-Net-based and quantifies key histological components of the MASH-score, including steatosis, fibrosis, inflammation and ballooning. Additionally, we determined novel features that are inaccessible through manual histology, like the distribution of fat droplet sizes, nuclear aspect ratio and heatmaps. qHisto parameters showed strong positive correlations with conventional histology scores (fat: R = 0.91, inflammation: R = 0.70, ballooning: R = 0.47) and with hepatic fat fraction by magnetic resonance imaging ( R = 0.87). Our novel scores showed that nuclei deformation is driven by large fat droplets rather than the overall amount of fat. A key advantage of our method is spatially resolved, precise histological quantification to provide detailed assessment of disease severity. By automating time-consuming and repetitive readouts, qHisto improves standardisation and reproducibility of MASH/MASLD feature quantification and provides scalable, slide-wide analysis that supports histopathologists and enhances clinical assessment.

records.title: Ideal Point Fusion for Reliable Morphometry of Lunar Regolith Particles
records.abstract: Lunar regolith particle morphology is critical for particle classification and representative sample selection. Morphometric measurements also provide key parameters for discrete element modeling and the development of regolith simulants with controlled particle shapes. However, their accuracy depends directly on segmentation quality. This study investigates whether combining measurements from complementary segmentation models can improve accuracy across morphological descriptors. The fusion leaves the source masks unchanged. The objective is to develop and evaluate Morphology-Aware Ideal-Point Fusion (MIPF). MIPF evaluates each model in three dimensions: region completeness, boundary accuracy, and false-positive suppression. Ideal-point analysis assigns higher scores to models closer to the best observed performance and farther from the worst. MIPF uses descriptor-specific weights for these scores to determine each model’s contribution. Area-based indices place more weight on region completeness, while contour-based indices emphasize boundary accuracy. MIPF then retains the two highest-weighted models and combines their measurements without generating a new mask. In a ground-truth comparison based on dataset-level means for 15 morphological indices, MIPF ranks first for six indices and second for the remaining nine, giving an average rank of 1.60. Its median relative error is 11.56%, compared with 12.96% for U-Mamba, 13.73% for nnU-Net, 15.30% for OffSeg, and 31.18% for SegFormer. Although MIPF does not minimize the error for every index, it achieves the most consistent overall performance and reduces the dependence of aggregate morphometric results on any single segmentation model.
